decisions.justification: The “Freshness” question offered automatic next-export freshness versus an explicit fresh mode, and the user selected “Next export.”
The “Freshness” options explicitly contrasted freshness on the next export, within 15 minutes, or only when requested.
The selected “Next export” option explicitly retained cached ranges while the source was unchanged, after the question cited the nightly ten-minute constraint.
The “Scope” question offered preserving the existing CLI versus adding a fresh flag, and the user selected “Cache freshness only.”
The “Mid-update” question asked whether an invocation restarts, finishes its started snapshot, or fails, and the user chose the consistent started snapshot.
The user was directly asked what should happen when a newer valid orders file lands during export and chose “Finish started snapshot.”
The agent selected a filesystem-stat source marker without asking the user to choose among metadata, hashing, or bypassing cache on the fresh path, and repository facts did not prove that policy.
The “Bad source” question offered fail clearly versus serving stale cache, and the user selected “Fail clearly.”
The “Mid-update” options included restarting once, finishing the existing snapshot without retry, or refusing the overlap, and the user chose no retry.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The session declared a bounded path before questioning, used repository-specific evidence, and obtained clear choices for nearly every behavioral policy. It did not ask the material change-detection question and silently chose stat-derived identity; the final test also changes file size, so it does not exercise the rubric’s same-size, preserved-mtime risk.
